questions.question: Name the three essential parts of an electric circuit and identify each in a torch. Explain what is used up and what is not used up as the torch is used.
questions.expected_answer: Energy source: the cells (store chemical potential energy). Conductors/path: the metal strips, springs and wires (and switch). Load: the bulb, which transfers energy to light and heat. The electric charges are not used up; the same charges circulate round the closed circuit, collecting energy in the cells and transferring it in the bulb. What is used up is the stored chemical energy in the cells, as the chemicals react; the cells go flat when it is used up.

questions.question: Distinguish between a closed and an open circuit. Explain how a switch works and why a break anywhere in a single-loop circuit makes the bulb go out.
questions.expected_answer: A closed (complete) circuit is an unbroken conducting path from one terminal of the source through the components back to the other terminal, so charges can flow. An open circuit has a gap, so charges cannot flow. A switch has two metal contacts: on, they touch and close the circuit; off, they are separated by an air gap (insulator) and open it. In a single loop, the charges must flow all the way round; a gap anywhere stops the flow everywhere in the loop, so the bulb goes out wherever the gap is.

questions.question: Give the input and output energies of a filament bulb, a kettle and a fan. Use the filament bulb to explain useful and wasted energy and the conservation of energy, and explain why LED lamps are better.
questions.expected_answer: Input for all: electrical energy. Bulb: light (useful) and heat (wasted). Kettle: heat (useful) and a little sound. Fan: kinetic energy (useful), sound and heat (wasted). In a filament bulb only about 5% of the input becomes light; about 95% becomes heat, which is wasted. All the input energy is accounted for (light + heat = input), so energy is conserved, not destroyed. An LED transfers a much larger fraction of its input to light, so less energy (and money) is needed for the same light and electricity demand is reduced.
